items.title: 0.4 Parity harness
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: ADR 052 (supersedes ADR 048, becomes Accepted), DD-012, DD-013, DD-014

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Make ADR 052 executable: an endpoint's behaviour is written down as scenarios — requests and the responses Apache Atlas 2.4.0 gives, read from its source and its own tests — and every scenario runs as a test against Aurelius Atlas, with its result in the test report.

  • libs/python/aurelius-atlas-parity (aurelius_atlas_parity):
    • the scenario format, *.scenario.yaml;
    • load_scenarios, which turns a directory of scenarios into pytest parameters, one test per scenario, and run_scenario, which sends its requests through an httpx.AsyncClient and compares the responses;
    • a pytest plugin that records each scenario's endpoints and deviations as test properties.
  • aurelius-atlas-trace: the trace file carries test properties; check refuses a scenario that names an unknown deviation; report gets a section per endpoint.
  • Proof: the harness's own tests run scenarios against a small sample ASGI application.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Scenarios for real Atlas endpoints 0.5 (admin endpoints) and each increment A running Apache Atlas, or recording from one not planned (ADR 052) Order-insensitive comparison of arrays the first increment that needs it Multipart and form request bodies 6.3 (import and export)

items.title: The scenario format
items.text: Id Rule SCN-01 A scenario is one YAML file named *.scenario.yaml with a name, a non-empty source list citing where in Atlas 2.4.0 the expectation was read, optional rules and covers, and one or more stages SCN-02 A stage has an optional name, a request (method, url, optional params, headers and a json or text body) and a response (status, optional headers, a json or text body, and, with a json body, volatile paths, save names and deviations) SCN-03 A file that does not parse or does not match the format fails the collection of the test module that loads it, naming the file and the problem; unknown keys, keys given twice and unquoted dates are problems SCN-04 Each scenario becomes one test whose id is its path below the scenario directory without the suffix; its rules and covers become a covers marker of that test

items.title: Running and comparing
items.text: Id Rule SCN-05 Stages run in order through the httpx.AsyncClient the test gives; the first stage whose response differs fails the scenario, and later stages do not run SCN-06 save stores the value at a path of the response under a name; {name} in a later stage's request or expected response is replaced by it, a string that is exactly {name} takes the value with its JSON type SCN-07 A path is a JSONPath subset: $, .name, ['name'], [n] and [*]; a save path must match exactly one value, and an unknown name in {name} fails the stage SCN-08 The status is compared exactly; each listed header is compared by exact value under a case-insensitive name; headers that are not listed are not compared SCN-09 A json body is compared exactly: the same keys, arrays of the same length in the same order, equal numbers, and booleans and null only equal themselves; a text body must be identical; no body means an empty body SCN-10 At a volatile path, the value is not compared, but the field must be present in the response exactly where the expectation has it SCN-11 A failing stage reports every difference of its response, each with its path, the expected and the actual value

items.title: Deviations
items.text: Id Rule SCN-12 The expectation in a scenario is the Atlas response; a deliberate difference is a deviations entry of the stage's response with a DV-NN id, a path, and the Aurelius value or absent: true, applied to the expectation before comparing; a deviation that changes nothing fails the stage SCN-13 aurelius-atlas-trace check lists every scenario that names a deviation id the deviations table does not define

items.title: The report
items.text:
Id Rule SCN-14 The trace file records every test's user_properties after collection; each scenario test carries one parity.endpoint property per endpoint its stages call (method and URL before substitution, without the query) and one parity.deviation property per deviation id SCN-15 The report has a section with one row per endpoint: its scenarios with their outcomes and deviations, with the same statuses as rules; the Markdown summary counts endpoints SCN-16 Every run of a scenario starts with {run} saved: a value unique to that run, in letters and digits, for names a scenario creates (added by 2.4, DD-055)

Rule SCN-01 is ADR 052 R1: a scenario without a citation is not a scenario. The format borrows the stage shape of Tavern, and scenarios run as ordinary parametrised pytest tests (DD-012). Rules SCN-09 and SCN-10 make the comparison exact (DD-013), and SCN-14 carries scenario facts to the report through the trace file (DD-014).

items.title: Java origin
items.text: None: this is conversion tooling, not Atlas behaviour. The scenarios of later increments cite the release-2.4.0 tag of github.com/apache/atlas, for example webapp/src/main/java/org/apache/atlas/web/resources/AdminResource.java#getVersion or webapp/src/test/resources/json/search-parameters/entity-filters.json.

items.title: 0.5 Server skeleton
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-015, DD-016; DV-03, DV-04, DV-05; relies on ADR 052, DD-001, DD-002

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The Aurelius Atlas server exists and answers the admin endpoints that tell a client, a load balancer or the dashboard whether Atlas is there and how it is configured.

  • apps/aurelius-atlas-server (aurelius_atlas_server), a FastAPI application:
    • settings read once at start-up, the Elasticsearch store opened for the server's lifetime;
    • the Atlas error body and JSON media type, shared by every later endpoint;
    • GET /api/atlas/admin/version, /status, /session, /liveness and /readiness;
    • a container image, nx serve against the dev store, and nx e2e running the scenarios against the image over HTTPS.
  • Parity scenarios for the five endpoints in apps/aurelius-atlas-server/scenarios/admin/, run in-process by the unit tests and over HTTPS by the end-to-end tests.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by The dashboards at / and /n/ 0.6 Removing the template's example projects after the plan (DD-019) Authentication; the session's user, groups and permissions 6.1, 6.2 Metrics (/admin/metrics) and the other admin endpoints 6.4 and the increments that own them High availability states (PASSIVE, BECOMING_ACTIVE, …) not planned

items.title: The server
items.text: Id Rule SRV-01 Settings are read once at start-up from environment variables prefixed AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_; a missing or invalid setting stops the start-up and names the setting SRV-02 The server opens the Elasticsearch store before it accepts requests and does not start when the store cannot be opened; it closes the store when it stops SRV-03 The server listens on port 21000 unless configured otherwise, and serves HTTPS when both a certificate and a key are configured; configuring only one is an error SRV-04 An Atlas error is answered with its HTTP status and the body {"errorCode": ..., "errorMessage": ...}, plus errorCause when the error has a cause SRV-05 JSON responses of the Atlas API carry the media type application/json; charset=UTF-8

items.title: The admin endpoints
items.text:
Id Rule ADM-01 GET /api/atlas/admin/version answers 200 with Version, Revision, Name and Description; Aurelius Atlas names itself and its own release and revision (DV-03) ADM-02 GET /api/atlas/admin/status answers 200 with {"Status": "ACTIVE"} while the server runs ADM-03 GET /api/atlas/admin/liveness answers 200 with the text Service is live while the server runs ADM-04 GET /api/atlas/admin/readiness answers 200 with the text Service is ready to accept requests when the store is healthy, and otherwise 500 with error ATLAS-500-00-001 and message Internal server error Service not ready to accept client requests ADM-05 GET /api/atlas/admin/session answers 200 with the user interface settings of Atlas 2.4.0 at their defaults, userName null, groups empty and both entity permissions false (DV-04), the time zone ids (DV-05) and a _csrfToken of 20 letters and digits

Rules ADM-01 to ADM-05 are those of AdminResource; their parity scenarios cite it method by method. SRV-02 makes a server that cannot reach its only store fail at start-up rather than answer every request with an error (DD-016); the application layout is DD-015.

items.title: Java origin
items.text:
Apache Atlas release-2.4.0:

  • webapp/.../web/resources/AdminResource.java: getVersion, getStatus, getUserProfile, serviceLiveliness, serviceReadiness, the session defaults in the constructor
  • webapp/.../web/errors/AtlasBaseExceptionMapper.java: the error body
  • intg/.../AtlasErrorCode.java: INTERNAL_ERROR
  • webapp/.../web/util/Servlets.java: JSON_MEDIA_TYPE
  • webapp/.../web/filters/AtlasCSRFPreventionFilter.java: the CSRF defaults the session reports
  • intg/.../AtlasConfiguration.java: the defaults of the session's feature switches

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
• DV-03: version reports Aurelius Atlas, not Apache Atlas.
  • DV-04: no authentication until 6.1; the session has no user.
  • DV-05: the session's time zone ids come from the IANA database.

items.title: Acceptance
items.text:

  • apps/aurelius-atlas-server/tests/ — the scenarios in-process (ADM-01 to ADM-05), settings and start-up (SRV-01 to SRV-03), errors and media type (SRV-04, SRV-05), readiness with a store that is down (ADM-04).
  • apps/aurelius-atlas-server/e2e/ — the same scenarios over HTTPS against the container image connected to the dev store (nx e2e aurelius-atlas-server).

items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-017, DD-018, DD-019; relies on DD-001, ADR 046

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The two Apache Atlas 2.4.0 user interfaces are served by the Aurelius Atlas server where Atlas serves them: dashboardv2 at / and dashboardv3 at /n/ (DD-001).

  • apps/aurelius-atlas-dashboard: the dashboardv2 and dashboardv3 source of the release-2.4.0 tag, vendored unchanged apart from the patches listed in its PATCHES.md, with a build target that compiles both in a hardened Node container.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by The data the dashboards show (types, entities, search, lineage, …) 1.x to 5.x The login page (login.jsp) and the redirect to it 6.1 Changes to the dashboards' behaviour or look not planned (ADR 046, DD-001)

Until those increments land, the dashboards load and show errors for every call the server does not answer yet. That is the expected state, not a deviation.

items.title: Semantics
items.text:

items.title: 1.1 Typedef models
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-020, DD-021, DD-022; relies on DD-002, DD-013, ADR 046

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The data shapes of Atlas type definitions, in a new library without I/O, libs/python/aurelius-atlas-model (package aurelius_atlas_model, DD-002):

  • the six type definitions: enum, struct, classification, entity, relationship and business metadata, with their parts (attribute, constraint, enum element, relationship end and relationship attribute definitions);
  • the type definition header and AtlasTypesDef, the body of /v2/types/typedefs;
  • reading them from and writing them to the JSON Atlas uses on its REST API, and the small helpers the Java classes offer (attribute and element lookup, super types, built-in type names).

No endpoint changes; the server does not use the library yet.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Resolving type names, supertypes and constraints; validation errors 1.2 Defaults the type registry fills in (relationship category, tags, …) 1.3 Storing type definitions; the built-in models at start-up 1.4, 1.5 /v2/types/...; malformed bodies answered with Atlas's error and 400 1.6 Order-insensitive comparison of set-valued arrays in parity scenarios 1.6 (DD-013) The paged lists (AtlasStructDefs, … built on PList) 1.6

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
"Reading" is what Atlas's Jackson mapper does with a REST request body; "writing" is what it puts in a response. Atlas serialises the models with Jackson 2.12 (AtlasJsonProvider, no date or naming customisation) and the annotations on each class (DD-020).

Id Rule TDM-01 Every field is read and written under the name of its Java getter: isOptional, valuesMinCount, includeInNotification, endDef1, relationshipAttributeDefs, businessAttributeDefs, … TDM-02 Writing leaves out a field whose value is null; an empty list, set or map is written TDM-03 Reading ignores fields the model does not have TDM-04 Each type definition writes its category (ENUM, STRUCT, CLASSIFICATION, ENTITY, RELATIONSHIP, BUSINESS_METADATA), fixed by its kind; a category in the input is ignored. The header reads and writes category like any field TDM-05 createTime and updateTime are written as milliseconds since the epoch, and read from such a number or from an ISO-8601 date-time string (DD-022) TDM-06 attributeDefs (struct and its kinds), elementDefs (enum), superTypes (classification, entity) and entityTypes (classification) are never null: missing, null or empty reads as empty TDM-07 Of attribute definitions with the same name, compared without case, only the last is kept, at its own position; an attribute definition without a name is dropped TDM-08 Of enum elements with the same value, compared without case, only the last is kept, at its own position; an element without a value is dropped TDM-09 superTypes, subTypes and entityTypes hold each name once (DD-021) TDM-10 An attribute definition without them reads as isOptional false, cardinality SINGLE, valuesMinCount and valuesMaxCount -1, isUnique, isIndexable and includeInNotification false, searchWeight -1; an explicit null reads as false or 0, as in Java TDM-11 An empty constraints list reads as null and is not written; options maps are copied TDM-12 A relationship end without them reads as cardinality SINGLE, isContainer and isLegacyAttribute false; a relationship definition keeps relationshipCategory, propagateTags and its ends null when they are not given TDM-13 AtlasTypesDef reads each of its six lists as empty when missing and keeps an explicit null, which it does not write TDM-14 Type categories, cardinalities, index types, relationship categories and tag propagations are read and written by their Java names, with case; any other value is rejected TDM-15 Scalars are coerced as Jackson 2.12 coerces them by default: a number into a string field, a numeric or boolean string into a number or boolean field. A value that cannot be coerced, such as an object where a string is expected, is rejected with an error that names the field TDM-16 Attribute definitions and enum elements are found, replaced and removed by name or value without case; super types and entity types by exact name. Options and constraint parameters are read and set by exact key, a constraint's type is compared without case, and the isSoftReference and isAppendOnPartialUpdate options are true only for the value true, without case TDM-17 AtlasTypesDef is empty when all six lists are empty or null, and tells whether it holds a type definition of a kind by exact name TDM-18 A header made from a type definition carries its guid, name, category and serviceType TDM-19 array<T> and map<K,V> type names are built as Atlas builds them, and the primitive, built-in and relationship attribute type names are Atlas's TDM-20 Writing a model and reading the result gives an equal model; the type definitions of Atlas's 0010-base_model.json and 0011-glossary_model.json read without error

TDM-06 to TDM-13 are the Java setters' and constructors' normalisations, which run when Jackson reads a body: a client that sends a duplicate attribute or no cardinality sees the normalised definition in the response.

items.title: 1.2 Type registry
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-023, DD-024, DD-025; relies on DD-002, DD-020

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The registry that turns type definitions into resolved types, in a new library without I/O, libs/python/aurelius-atlas-typesystem (package aurelius_atlas_typesystem, DD-002):

  • the registry: the built-in types, lookup by name and GUID, the definitions per kind, and updates made on a transient copy that is committed or discarded;
  • the types: built-in, array, map, enum and struct, and for classification, entity, relationship and business metadata definitions their own attributes, resolved as a struct's are;
  • attribute resolution: attribute types, cardinality, the classification and business metadata ban, and the ownedRef and inverseRef constraints;
  • the Atlas error codes these raise, in the model library, where every layer can raise them (DD-023).

No endpoint changes; the server does not use the registry yet.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Super and sub types, inherited attributes, root types, classification entityTypes 1.3 Relationship ends and relationship attributes; business metadata applicableEntityTypes 1.3 Rejecting duplicate or reserved type names, and type names already in use 1.4 (the store) Validating, normalising and defaulting attribute values 2.1 (DD-025) JanusGraph property names, index field names and index-query escaping dropped (DD-025)

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Id Rule TRG-01 A new registry holds the built-in types boolean, byte, short, int, long, float, double, biginteger, bigdecimal, date and string (category PRIMITIVE) and objectid (OBJECT_ID_TYPE), all with service type atlas_core TRG-02 A registered name answers its type. An unregistered array<T> or map<K,V> name is built on demand from its element, key and value types, splitting a map's at its first comma; an array built so has cardinality LIST and no element counts TRG-03 An unknown type name fails with TYPE_NAME_NOT_FOUND (404) and an unknown GUID with TYPE_GUID_NOT_FOUND (404), each naming what was asked for TRG-04 Definitions are found by name and by GUID, per kind and across all kinds; each kind lists its definitions, names and types, and the registry lists all type names, all types and all service types TRG-05 The registry changes only through a transient copy taken under the update lock. Committing makes the copy's types the registry's; releasing without committing discards them. The lock is re-entrant; waiting longer than its timeout fails with FAILED_TO_OBTAIN_TYPE_UPDATE_LOCK (500) (DD-024) TRG-06 Adding a definition registers it by name and, when it has one, by GUID. A later definition with the same name replaces the earlier one, a built-in type included TRG-07 Updating replaces the definition with the given GUID or name; a definition updated without a target is found by its GUID, else by its name, else ignored TRG-08 Removing by GUID or by name removes the definition under both. Removing the definitions of an AtlasTypesDef removes each by its GUID when it has one, else by its name. The transient copy records what was added, updated and removed, in order TRG-09 After every change the copy resolves every type again; the first failure is raised and nothing reaches the registry TRG-10 Each attribute's type must resolve. LIST and SET cardinality need an array type, else INVALID_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_FOR_CARDINALITY (400); the array then takes the attribute's cardinality and value counts. An attribute whose type, array element or map value is a classification or business metadata type fails with ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_INVALID (400) TRG-11 An attribute's qualified name is Type.attribute, or its name when that contains a dot. An entity type in an attribute becomes objectid of that entity type, also inside arrays and maps; such an array or map is a new one, so an array keeps cardinality LIST and no value counts, as in Java. The attribute is an object reference when its type, array element or map value is objectid TRG-12 ownedRef needs an entity type (or an array or map of one), else CONSTRAINT_OWNED_REF_ATTRIBUTE_INVALID_TYPE. inverseRef needs one too (CONSTRAINT_INVERSE_REF_ATTRIBUTE_INVALID_TYPE), a non-blank attribute parameter (CONSTRAINT_MISSING_PARAMS), that attribute defined on the referenced entity type (CONSTRAINT_INVERSE_REF_INVERSE_ATTRIBUTE_NON_EXISTING) and of an entity type (CONSTRAINT_INVERSE_REF_INVERSE_ATTRIBUTE_INVALID_TYPE), all 400; the inverse attribute is then linked TRG-13 A type's attributes are looked up by exact name; its unique attributes are those whose definition is unique TRG-14 An enum type finds its elements by value without case and by ordinal; its default is the definition's defaultValue, else the first element's value TRG-15 Every error carries Atlas's HTTP status, error code and message, with {0}, {1}, … filled in from its parameters in order TRG-16 Classification, entity, relationship and business metadata types resolve their own attributes as a struct type does

TRG-06 to TRG-08 copy the registry's own behaviour: it accepts what it is given. The checks that a name is new, not reserved and not in use are the type definition store's (AtlasTypeDefGraphStore), ported in 1.4.

items.title: 1.3 Type hierarchies
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-026, DD-027; relies on DD-021, DD-024, DD-025

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The parts of the type system that link types to each other, in aurelius-atlas-typesystem:

  • entity and classification hierarchies: super types, all super and sub types, inherited attributes, the root types with the system attributes, and the sub types written back to the definitions;
  • the entity type's derived attributes: header and minimal-info attributes, the display-text attribute, owned references and whether the type is internal;
  • the entity types a classification may be applied to;
  • relationship types: their ends, label and the relationship attributes they add to entity types, which are inherited and written back to the entity definitions with the tag-propagation edges;
  • business metadata types: their attributes, the entity types they apply to, and the business attributes written back to the entity definitions;
  • Atlas error messages formatted as Java's MessageFormat formats them.

No endpoint changes.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Dynamic attributes (dynAttribute: templates) and their evaluation order 2.4 (DD-026) The root entity type's lookup of business attributes for search 4.1 (DD-026) Logging relationship definitions an entity attribute lacks (reportMissingRelationshipDef) not ported Index-query strings of type names (getTypeAndAllSubTypesQryStr) dropped (DD-025)

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
Id Rule THY-01 An entity type's super types must be entity types and a classification's must be classifications, else INCOMPATIBLE_SUPERTYPE (400) with the super type's name first and the type's second, as Java passes them THY-02 A type that reaches itself through its super types fails with CIRCULAR_REFERENCE (400), naming the type and the types visited on the way, as [A, B] THY-03 A type's attributes are those of all its super types, depth first in the order the super types are given, then its own. A name defined by two different types of the hierarchy fails with ATTRIBUTE_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS_IN_ANOTHER_PARENT_TYPE (400); a super type reached twice is not a conflict THY-04 Each type knows its super types, all super types and the sub types and all sub types that every other type's super types give it, each also with the type itself. Sub types are written to the definition's subTypes THY-05 __ENTITY_ROOT and __CLASSIFICATION_ROOT hold Atlas's system attributes (__guid, __typeName, __timestamp, …); every entity and classification type finds them by name after its own and inherited attributes. Root types are not registered, and their attribute names are not qualified THY-06 An entity type's header attributes are its unique attributes and name, description, owner and createTime; its minimal-info attributes add those its schemaAttributes option lists. Its display-text attribute is its displayTextAttribute option, else a direct super type's option, else any super type's, when that names an attribute. It is internal when __internal is among its super types. Its owned references are the attributes and relationship attributes with ownedRef THY-07 A classification applies to its entityTypes and all their sub types (an unknown name fails with TYPE_NAME_NOT_FOUND), narrowed by what its super types allow. Super types whose allowed types do not overlap fail with CLASSIFICATIONDEF_PARENTS_ENTITYTYPES_DISJOINT, and own types outside them with CLASSIFICATIONDEF_ENTITYTYPES_NOT_PARENTS_SUBSET (400); with no own types it applies where its super types allow; with no restriction anywhere, to every entity type THY-08 A relationship's two ends need a type (MISSING_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE, endDef1.type) that is an entity type (RELATIONSHIPDEF_INVALID_END_TYPE) and a name. No end may be LIST; not both ends may be containers; a container needs AGGREGATION or COMPOSITION, which in turn need a container; a COMPOSITION end with SET must be the container. Each breach has its Atlas code (400) THY-09 A relationship's label is its relationshipLabel, else r: and its name when neither end is a legacy attribute, else __ and the qualified name of the legacy end's attribute THY-10 Each end adds a relationship attribute named after the end to its entity type. When the type has no attribute of that name, the attribute is new: it holds the other end's type (array<…> for SET), with the end's cardinality, optional except on a composition's child end, and ownedRef on a composition's container end. Otherwise the existing attribute is used and marked legacy. Each has the relationship's name, edge label and an edge direction (OUT, IN or BOTH) THY-11 Sub types inherit relationship attributes; the first a type gets per attribute and relationship stays. They are written to the entity definition's relationshipAttributeDefs with their relationship's name and legacy flag, and with isAppendOnPartialUpdate when the type's appendRelationshipsOnPartialUpdate option lists them. A relationship's label is the type's tag-propagation edge when its propagateTags sends classifications from that type THY-12 A business metadata attribute may not hold a struct, classification or business metadata type, nor an array or map of one (BUSINESS_METADATA_DEF_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_INVALID); its applicableEntityTypes option must name entity types; a string attribute needs a maxStrLength option (MISSING_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE). Business attributes are added to the entity types they apply to and their sub types, found as bm.attribute, and written to the entity definition's businessAttributeDefs THY-13 Error messages follow MessageFormat: an apostrophe starts or ends quoted text, which is copied as is and loses the apostrophe, and two apostrophes are one; collection parameters are written as [a, b]

THY-04, THY-11 and THY-12 change the definitions the registry holds, as Java does. The definitions Types REST returns (1.6) therefore carry subTypes, relationshipAttributeDefs and businessAttributeDefs.

items.title: 1.4 Typedef store
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-028, DD-029, DD-030, DV-06; relies on ADR 047, DD-002, DD-005, DD-024

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Type definitions are kept in Elasticsearch and loaded into the type registry when the server starts, in a new library libs/python/aurelius-atlas-core (package aurelius_atlas_core, the -core layer of DD-002):

  • the typedef store: create, update and delete type definitions, with the checks Atlas's store makes and its registry does not (unique and well-formed names, no attribute removed, no type deleted while something refers to it), and the audit fields;
  • the stored form: what Atlas keeps of a definition, which is what it answers with afterwards;
  • persistence in one Elasticsearch document, written with optimistic concurrency (DD-028, DD-029);
  • the server loads the stored definitions into its registry at start-up and keeps it in step with other processes.

No endpoint changes: /v2/types arrives in 1.6.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Atlas's built-in models (addons/models), the model patches and createUpdate 1.5 /v2/types/..., search filters over type definitions, authorization of type reads 1.6, 6.2 Refusing to delete a type that entities or classifications still use 2.2 (DD-030) Attribute names that are DSL keywords (atlas.types.allowReservedKeywords) not ported (*)

(*) Atlas allows them by default; the check is off unless that setting is changed.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule TDS-01 Creating definitions resolves them with every stored type first (TRG-09); an unknown type name or GUID found then fails with BAD_REQUEST (400) carrying the resolution's message. Nothing is stored unless every definition passes TDS-02 A definition's name must match [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_ ]*, optionally prefixed with __, else TYPE_NAME_INVALID_FORMAT (400); a name already stored fails with TYPE_ALREADY_EXISTS (409), and a name another kind holds with TYPE_MATCH_FAILED (400), naming Atlas's legacy kind (CLASS, TRAIT, STRUCT, …) TDS-03 A created definition gets typeVersion 1.0, version 1, a random GUID and the current time as createTime and updateTime, each only when it has none; its description defaults to its name; createdBy and updatedBy are the current user (none until 6.1, DV-06) TDS-04 Every attribute must have a name and a type name (MISSING_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE); a type it names that is neither built in nor stored fails with UNKNOWN_TYPE (400). A struct needs attributes (BAD_REQUEST, Missing attributes for structdef); a business metadata attribute's name must match the type name pattern (ATTRIBUTE_NAME_INVALID_CHARS). An enum needs elements, and each element a value and an ordinal (MISSING_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE, values and elementValue) TDS-05 An attribute is stored in Atlas's form and read back from it: cardinality and counts become isOptional, valuesMinCount and valuesMaxCount as Atlas's multiplicity gives them (an optional single value reads 0 and 1, an unbounded list or set 2147483647); only ownedRef and inverseRef constraints are kept, in that order; options, default value, description, display name, search weight and index type are kept TDS-06 A stored relationship without a category is ASSOCIATION, and without propagateTags is NONE; its label and ends are kept as given TDS-07 Updating finds each definition by its GUID when it has one, else by its name (TYPE_GUID_NOT_FOUND or TYPE_NAME_NOT_FOUND, 404, mapped to BAD_REQUEST while resolving, as TDS-01). The name, the kind and the creation fields stay; blank fields keep their stored value; version goes up by one and updateTime and updatedBy are set TDS-08 An update may not remove an attribute (ATTRIBUTE_DELETION_NOT_SUPPORTED), change an attribute's type (BAD_REQUEST, Data type update for attribute is not supported) or add a mandatory one (CANNOT_ADD_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE); a relationship's name, category and ends may not change (RELATIONSHIPDEF_INVALID_*_UPDATE, with Java's text of the ends); a business metadata attribute may not lose applicable entity types (APPLICABLE_ENTITY_TYPES_DELETION_NOT_SUPPORTED); super types may not be removed (SUPERTYPE_REMOVAL_NOT_SUPPORTED), nor some of a classification's entity types (ENTITYTYPE_REMOVAL_NOT_SUPPORTED), though all of them may. A classification's entity types must be stored entity types, on create too (CLASSIFICATIONDEF_INVALID_ENTITYTYPES) TDS-09 Deleting finds each definition by GUID, else name, and fails with TYPE_HAS_REFERENCES (409) while another stored type refers to it as a super type, an attribute type or a classification's entity type, and an entity type with TYPE_HAS_RELATIONSHIPS (409) while a relationship ends on it. References from definitions deleted in the same request do not count, so a relationship and the types it ends on may be deleted together TDS-10 A change is written only after the transient registry resolved it, then committed to the registry; when the write fails, nothing is committed and the stored document is unchanged TDS-11 The stored definitions are one document whose Elasticsearch version guards every write: a write based on an older version fails, the process reloads and the change is retried once, else FAILED_TO_OBTAIN_TYPE_UPDATE_LOCK (500) (DD-028, DD-029) TDS-12 At start-up the server loads the stored definitions into its registry, dropping a second definition with the same name and an ownedRef constraint on an attribute that refers to no entity type, as Atlas's rectifyTypeErrorsIfAny does; with nothing stored, the registry holds the built-in types only TDS-13 A process whose registry is older than the stored document reloads it before it changes types, and at least every AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_TYPEDEF_REFRESH_SECONDS (default 5) before it answers

items.title: 1.5 Built-in models and patches
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-031, DD-032, DD-033, DV-07, DV-08; relies on DD-028, DD-029, DV-06

items.title: Scope
items.text:
When the server starts, it loads Atlas's built-in type definitions (addons/models) and their patches into the typedef store of 1.4, as AtlasTypeDefStoreInitializer does:

  • the 2.4.0 models, vendored unchanged into aurelius-atlas-core (DD-032), read from a directory the server can be pointed at (AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_MODELS_DIR);
  • each model file creates the types not yet stored and updates those whose typeVersion is newer (createUpdateTypesDef);
  • the typedef patches, with the nine patch actions of Atlas 2.4.0, and the record of each patch's outcome, kept in the typedef document (DD-031);
  • processes that start together apply each file and each patch once (DD-033).

No endpoint changes: the loaded types are served by /v2/types in 1.6.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by /v2/types/... 1.6 admin/patches, and the Java patches (AtlasPatchManager, UniqueAttributePatch, …) 2.2 Setting the default of a new mandatory attribute, and new super types, on existing entities 2.2 Deferring the load until an instance becomes active (atlas.server.ha.enabled) not ported The legacy TypesResource (/api/atlas/types), the other caller of createUpdateTypesDef not ported

AddMandatoryAttributesPatch and SuperTypesUpdatePatch, which ADD_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE and ADD_SUPER_TYPES schedule, change entities; without entities there is nothing for them to do until 2.2. High availability is replaced by DD-029 and DD-033: every process may load the models.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule MDL-01 The models directory is read in name order: each sub-directory except one named patches, then the directory itself. Of each, the files are loaded in name order, then the files of its patches sub-directory are applied in name order. Other entries are ignored; a missing directory loads nothing. Names compare as Java's String.compareTo MDL-02 A model file is an AtlasTypesDef; an empty one is skipped. Its definitions whose name is not registered, as any kind or built-in, are created. A definition whose name is registered as the same kind is updated when its typeVersion is greater than the registered one, compared as strings with an absent version less than any; the update keeps the registered attributes it lacks, appended in order, and an enum the registered elements it lacks MDL-03 A file's creations and updates are one change (createUpdateTypesDef): the updates replace the registered definitions without resolving, the creations are then resolved (an unknown type name fails with BAD_REQUEST, as TDS-01) and stored with TDS-02 to TDS-06, then the updates are stored with TDS-07 and TDS-08. Nothing of the file is stored unless all of it passes MDL-04 A model file that cannot be read, is not an AtlasTypesDef or fails MDL-03 is logged and skipped; loading goes on with the next file MDL-05 A patch file holds patches, a list of patches with id, description, action, typeName, applyToVersion, updateToVersion, params, attributeDefs, elementDefs, typeDefOptions, serviceType, attributeName and superTypes; other fields are ignored. A patch whose action is not one of the nine is logged and skipped. A patch whose id is recorded APPLIED or SKIPPED is not applied again; one recorded FAILED or UNKNOWN, or not recorded, is. A patch without an id is applied at every start and not recorded (DV-08) MDL-06 A patch ends APPLIED, SKIPPED or UNKNOWN as its action decides, or FAILED when it raises an Atlas error; its record (id, description, type TYPEDEF_PATCH, action, status, created and updated time) is written with its change (DD-031), and an existing record's created time stays. Any other error ends the patch file: its later patches are not applied, and the failing patch is not recorded MDL-07 Every action: a typeName that is not stored fails with PATCH_FOR_UNKNOWN_TYPE (action, type name). A patch applies when the type's typeVersion is absent, equals applyToVersion ignoring case, or starts with applyToVersion followed by .; otherwise it is SKIPPED. An applied patch sets typeVersion to updateToVersion and stores the type with TDS-07 and TDS-08. An action given a kind it does not handle fails with PATCH_NOT_APPLICABLE_FOR_TYPE (action, Java class name such as AtlasEnumDef) MDL-08 UPDATE_ENUMDEF (enums): adds each of elementDefs, replacing an element with the same value MDL-09 ADD_ATTRIBUTE (entities, classifications, structs, relationships) and UPDATE_ATTRIBUTE (entities, classifications, structs): add each of attributeDefs at the end, replacing an attribute with the same name. TDS-08 applies, so a changed attribute type or a new mandatory attribute fails MDL-10 ADD_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE (entities, classifications, structs): of attributeDefs, keeps those the type does not have that are mandatory, have a non-empty default value, have a primitive type and are not unique; an unknown attribute type fails with its registry error. With none kept the patch is SKIPPED; otherwise they are added, and the update may add mandatory attributes MDL-11 REMOVE_LEGACY_REF_ATTRIBUTES (relationships; any other kind ends UNKNOWN): the label is params.relationshipLabel, else __ and the qualified name of the attribute at the one legacy end, else the current label; with both ends legacy and no label it fails with PATCH_MISSING_RELATIONSHIP_LABEL. The ends swap when params.swapEnds is true, params.relationshipCategory replaces the category, and the attribute each end names is removed from its entity type. The relationship and both entity types are one update, in which attributes may be removed, the category may change and the ends may swap MDL-12 UPDATE_TYPEDEF_OPTIONS (any kind): fails with PATCH_INVALID_DATA without typeDefOptions, before the version check; merges them into the options, the patch's winning. SET_SERVICE_TYPE (any kind): sets the serviceType; without one the stored one stays, as TDS-07 keeps a blank serviceType MDL-13 UPDATE_ATTRIBUTE_METADATA (entities, structs): to the attributes named attributeName, ignoring case, applies each of params: searchWeight, a number, -1 or 1 to 10; indexType, DEFAULT or STRING, ignored when empty. Any other parameter or value is an error that ends the patch file (MDL-06). A type without the attribute still has the patch APPLIED MDL-14 ADD_SUPER_TYPES (entities): without superTypes the patch is SKIPPED, before the version check; otherwise each is added MDL-15 Each model file and each patch is one change of the typedef store (TDS-10, TDS-11), decided on the newest stored definitions and records: when another process wrote first, it is decided again, so processes starting together create, update and patch each type once (DD-033) MDL-16 The server loads the models after the stored definitions (TDS-12) and before it answers, from AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_MODELS_DIR, by default the vendored 2.4.0 models, which are byte-identical to addons/models of release-2.4.0. Built-in model types and patch records name no user (DV-07)

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The 26 endpoints of TypesREST under /api/atlas/v2/types, on the typedef store of 1.4 and the models of 1.5:

Endpoint Store operation GET typedef/name/{name}, GET typedef/guid/{guid} getByName, getByGuid GET {kind}def/name/{name}, GET {kind}def/guid/{guid} for enum, struct, classification, entity, relationship, businessmetadata get{Kind}DefByName, get{Kind}DefByGuid GET typedefs, GET typedefs/headers searchTypesDef POST typedefs, PUT typedefs, DELETE typedefs createTypesDef, updateTypesDef, deleteTypesDef DELETE typedef/name/{typeName} deleteTypeByName

The checks of the writes are 1.4's (TDS-01 to TDS-11); this increment adds the reads, the search filter and the HTTP side.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by TYPE_READ, TYPE_CREATE, TYPE_UPDATE and TYPE_DELETE checks and filtering of reads 6.2 createdBy and updatedBy of the logged-in user 6.1 Refusing to delete a type that entities use 2.2 (DD-030) The legacy TypesResource (/api/atlas/types) not ported

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule TYR-01 GET typedef/name/{name} answers the registered definition of that name, of any kind, as the registry holds it: with the subTypes, relationshipAttributeDefs and businessAttributeDefs resolution adds. A blank name fails with TYPE_NAME_INVALID (400), an unknown one with TYPE_NAME_NOT_FOUND (404), and a built-in, array or map type with SYSTEM_TYPE (400) naming its category (PRIMITIVE, OBJECT_ID_TYPE, ARRAY, MAP) TYR-02 GET typedef/guid/{guid} answers the definition with that GUID; a blank or unknown GUID fails with TYPE_GUID_NOT_FOUND (404) TYR-03 GET {kind}def/name/{name} and GET {kind}def/guid/{guid} answer the definition of that kind; a name or GUID that no definition of that kind has, including one of another kind, fails with TYPE_NAME_NOT_FOUND or TYPE_GUID_NOT_FOUND (404) TYR-04 On every GET by name or GUID, a name or GUID longer than 4096 characters fails with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH (400), naming name or guid, before the lookup TYR-05 GET typedefs answers every registered definition the filter keeps, as the registry holds them, in an AtlasTypesDef: enums, structs, classifications, entities, relationships, business metadata, each list sorted by name (DD-034, DV-09) TYR-06 The filter is the request's query parameters, each with its first value, with case-sensitive names: type keeps one kind (CLASS or ENTITY, TRAIT or CLASSIFICATION, STRUCT, ENUM, RELATIONSHIP, BUSINESS_METADATA, ignoring case; any other value keeps nothing); name the definition of that name; servicetype those of that service type; supertype the entity and classification types with it among all their super types; notsupertype, notservicetype and notname the others. A blank value filters nothing; other parameters are ignored TYR-07 excludeInternalTypesAndReferences=true, name and value ignoring case, adds notname=__internal and notsupertype=__internal. A notname given as well also applies; of two notsupertype values, the one first in the request applies (DV-09) TYR-08 GET typedefs/headers answers the header (guid, name, category, serviceType) of each definition GET typedefs would answer with the same filter, in its order TYR-09 POST typedefs creates (TDS-01 to TDS-06, TDS-10) and PUT typedefs updates (TDS-07, TDS-08, TDS-10) the definitions of the body; both answer 200 with the definitions as stored TYR-10 DELETE typedefs deletes the definitions of the body (TDS-09) and DELETE typedef/name/{typeName} the named one (TDS-09: blank TYPE_NAME_INVALID, unknown TYPE_NAME_NOT_FOUND, built-in SYSTEM_TYPE); both answer 204 with no body TYR-11 A write body that is not JSON, or not an AtlasTypesDef, fails with BAD_REQUEST (400) and Atlas's error body; unknown fields are ignored (DV-10) TYR-12 Every endpoint answers from a registry no older than AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_TYPEDEF_REFRESH_SECONDS (TDS-13); responses are Atlas JSON (TDM-02) as application/json; charset=UTF-8, and errors Atlas's error body (SRV-04)

items.text:
The data shapes of Atlas entities and their parts, in aurelius-atlas-model (package aurelius_atlas_model.instance, one module per Java class, DD-037):

Module Java class (org.apache.atlas.model) struct instance.AtlasStruct entity instance.AtlasEntity entity_status instance.AtlasEntity.Status entity_ext_info instance.AtlasEntity.AtlasEntityExtInfo entity_with_ext_info instance.AtlasEntity.AtlasEntityWithExtInfo entities_with_ext_info instance.AtlasEntity.AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo object_id instance.AtlasObjectId related_object_id instance.AtlasRelatedObjectId relationship_status instance.AtlasRelationship.Status classification instance.AtlasClassification time_boundary TimeBoundary entity_header instance.AtlasEntityHeader entity_headers instance.AtlasEntityHeaders entity_operation instance.EntityMutations.EntityOperation entity_mutation_response instance.EntityMutationResponse term_assignment_header glossary.relations.AtlasTermAssignmentHeader term_assignment_status glossary.enums.AtlasTermAssignmentStatus

The JSON conventions the typedef models already follow (AtlasModel, the timestamp, Java boolean and set types) move from typedef to a shared aurelius_atlas_model.base, which both packages import.

No endpoint changes; nothing uses the models yet.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Validating and normalising attribute values against their types; default values; equal values 2.1b Exact decimals in attribute values (USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS, DD-038) 2.1b The paged lists built on PList (AtlasEntities, AtlasClassifications, …) where used AtlasRelationship and AtlasRelationshipHeader 3.1 ClassificationAssociateRequest 3.3 EntityMutations and EntityMutation: no getter, so never on the REST API not ported AtlasCheckStateRequest, AtlasCheckStateResult, GuidMapping not planned

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
As in 1.1, "reading" is what Atlas's Jackson 2.12.7 mapper does with a REST request body, and "writing" is what it puts in a response. Jackson builds each model with its no-argument constructor, then calls the setter of each property in the order of the JSON; it writes each public getter, including a Boolean isXxx() getter, as property xxx.

Id Rule ENT-01 Every model reads and writes as the typedef models do: Java getter names (TDM-01), null fields left out and empty collections kept (TDM-02), unknown fields ignored (TDM-03), scalars coerced as Jackson coerces them (TDM-15); except the term assignment header (ENT-15) ENT-02 A struct has typeName and attributes. Attribute values are JSON values, kept as read: a null value stays in the map and is written. attributes that is missing stays null and is not written ENT-03 A struct tells whether it has an attribute, gets, sets and removes one by exact name; setting one on a struct without attributes creates the map ENT-04 An entity read without them has a new temporary GUID, - followed by digits, never the same twice in a process; isProxy and isIncomplete false; provenanceType and version 0; status null (init() clears the field's ACTIVE). A field given as null stays null ENT-05 An entity reads and writes guid, homeId, isIncomplete, provenanceType, status, createdBy, updatedBy, createTime, updateTime, version, relationshipAttributes, classifications, meanings, customAttributes, businessAttributes, labels and pendingTasks. It reads isProxy and writes it as proxy, as Jackson names the Boolean isProxy() getter ENT-06 createTime and updateTime are written as milliseconds since the epoch and read from such a number or an ISO-8601 date-time string, as TDM-05 ENT-07 labels and pendingTasks hold each value once, in first-seen order (DD-021), and may be null ENT-08 An entity gets, sets and tells whether it has a relationship attribute; gets and sets a business attribute by business metadata and attribute name, creating the maps it needs; appends classifications and meanings, creating the list ENT-09 Entity statuses (ACTIVE, DELETED, PURGED), relationship statuses (ACTIVE, DELETED), entity operations (CREATE, UPDATE, PARTIAL_UPDATE, DELETE, PURGE) and term assignment statuses (DISCOVERED to OTHER) are read and written by their Java names, with case; any other value is rejected ENT-10 Extended info maps GUIDs to referredEntities; it adds (an entity without a GUID is not added), gets, removes and finds a referred entity, and moves one to a new GUID. With one entity (entity) or a list (entities), finding by GUID also finds those, and compacting removes them from the referred entities ENT-11 An object id has guid, typeName and uniqueAttributes. Two object ids are equal by GUID when either has a non-empty one, otherwise by type name and unique attributes ENT-12 A related object id adds entityStatus, displayText, relationshipType, relationshipGuid, relationshipStatus, relationshipAttributes (a struct) and qualifiedName. Setting relationship attributes with a type name sets relationshipType to it; in a body, of the two the one that comes later wins ENT-13 A classification adds entityGuid, entityStatus (ACTIVE when not given), propagate, validityPeriods and removePropagationsOnEntityDelete, and appends a validity period. A time boundary has startTime, endTime and timeZone, as strings ENT-14 An entity header adds guid, status (ACTIVE when not given), displayText, classificationNames, classifications, meaningNames, meanings, isIncomplete (false when not given) and labels (as ENT-07). Made from an entity it takes the type name, attributes, GUID, status, classifications and isIncomplete, the classification names when it has any, and the labels when it has any; not the meanings ENT-15 A term assignment header has termGuid, relationGuid, description, displayText, expression, createdBy, steward, source, confidence, status and qualifiedName; it leaves out null and empty strings (@AtlasJSON, NON_EMPTY) but always writes confidence, an int that is 0 when not given or null ENT-16 The entity headers of bulk/headers map GUIDs to headers in guidHeaderMap ENT-17 A mutation response has mutatedEntities, headers by operation name, and guidAssignments. It also writes partialUpdatedEntities, the PARTIAL_UPDATE headers, when that operation is present (a getter without @JsonIgnore), and ignores it on reading. Adding an updated entity created in the same response records it as created; an entity is added once per operation, by GUID. It lists the headers of an operation, of an operation and type name, and finds the first, or one by type and attribute value ENT-18 Writing a model and reading the result gives an equal model; the entities of Atlas's hive hook test messages read without error and write back the same JSON

items.title: 2.1c Entity validation
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-042, DV-13; relies on DD-025, DD-037, DD-039, DD-040, DD-041

The last part of increment 2.1 (2.1a ported the entity models, 2.1b the value types): the value side of the struct, classification, entity and business metadata types, which check, normalise and default an instance attribute by attribute (DD-025).

items.title: Scope
items.text:
In aurelius-atlas-typesystem, finishing DD-041: the struct, classification, entity, relationship and business metadata types move out of types.py into one module each (struct_type, classification_type, entity_type, relationship_type, business_metadata_type, with attribute, edge_direction, hierarchy_type and type_names); types.py re-exports them. Then, for each type, createDefaultValue, isValidValue, getNormalizedValue, validateValue, their ForUpdate variants, areEqualValues, normalizeAttributeValues (and ForUpdate) and populateDefaultValues; the classification type's validity periods and the entity type's relationship attributes.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by The relationship type's own value checks: they take an AtlasRelationship 3.1 Business metadata attribute options on values (maxStrLength, validPattern): checked by the store, not the types 5.3 Using the types to validate entity writes (EntityGraphDiscovery, AtlasEntityStoreV2) 2.2, 2.4 Dynamic attributes (DD-026) 2.4

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
A value is a Java value as DD-040 holds it; a struct value is an AtlasStruct (or a subclass) or a map. "The attributes of a map" are its attributes map when it has a typeName key and an attributes map, else the map itself (AtlasTypeUtil.toStructAttributes); "its relationship attributes" likewise (toRelationshipAttributes), or none.

Id Rule EVL-01 A struct type takes a struct or a map. It is valid when each attribute the type itself defines has a valid value for its type, or no (null) value and is optional; super types check theirs. Any other value is invalid EVL-02 validateValue validates each such attribute's value as <name>.<attribute>; a mandatory attribute without a value adds <name>.<attribute>: mandatory attribute value missing in type <type>, unless the value is an entity with a relationship attribute of that name, or an incomplete entity, or a map whose relationship attributes have that name. A value that is no struct or map adds <name>=<value>: invalid value for type <type> EVL-03 The ForUpdate variants check, validate and normalise only the attributes that have a value and a definition in the type; a missing mandatory attribute is no error EVL-04 Normalising sets each attribute the type defines that is present to its normalised value (an invalid one becomes null; a null mandatory one the type's default), and adds each missing mandatory attribute with its default; the struct or map itself is the normalised value, or null when it is invalid EVL-05 The default of an attribute is its type's createDefaultValue of the attribute's defaultValue. populateDefaultValues sets every mandatory attribute to its default, replacing a value it has; createDefaultValue is a new struct, classification or entity of the type with its mandatory defaults, whatever value it is given EVL-06 Two struct values are equal when both are null, or both are structs or maps (read by Java's map constructor) of type names equal ignoring case whose every attribute is equal by its type. A string fails, as Java's ClassCastException EVL-07 A classification type checks its super types first, then its validity periods, then its own attributes. Each validity period of a classification (not of a map) has a known time zone (INVALID_TIMEBOUNDRY_TIMEZONE), a startTime and endTime that parse strictly as yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm:ss in that zone (INVALID_TIMEBOUNDRY_START_TIME, …END_TIME), and an end not before its start (INVALID_TIMEBOUNDRY_DATERANGE); validateValue adds each such message once. A known zone is a tz database id, one of Java's legacy three-letter ids, a custom GMT±h[h][[:]mm] offset or GMT; a period without a zone is in the server's zone (DD-042) EVL-08 An entity type checks its super types first, then its own attributes, then its relationship attributes. A relationship attribute is the type's attribute of that name for the value's relationship type (that of a related object id, a map's relationshipType, or the first element or map value that has one), else the first; a value of a relationship attribute whose type holds object ids or entities is checked by the object id type, any other by its type. validateValue adds a missing mandatory relationship attribute (not for an incomplete entity), and for a value that is no entity or map adds <name>: invalid value type '<Java class> EVL-09 Normalising an entity also normalises the value of each relationship attribute that holds object ids or entities EVL-10 A business metadata type takes every value; its default and every normalised value are null EVL-11 Atlas's type tests hold: testStructType…, testEntityType… and testClassificationType… (DefaultValue, IsValidValue, GetNormalizedValue, ValidateValue, TimebounderTimeZone) on ModelTestUtil's definitions, their random attribute types fixed; and TestAtlasEntity and TestAtlasClassification: a default value written to JSON, read back and normalised equals the original

items.title: Scope
items.text:
In aurelius-atlas-typesystem, one module per Java type class (DD-041):

Module Java class (org.apache.atlas.type) atlas_type AtlasType: the value contract every type has builtin/boolean_type … string_type AtlasBuiltInTypes.Atlas{Boolean,Byte,Short,Int,Long,Float,Double,BigInteger,BigDecimal,Date,String}Type builtin/object_id_type AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasObjectIdType enum_type, array_type, map_type AtlasEnumType, AtlasArrayType, AtlasMapType java the Java number and text conversions the types rely on values parsing a JSON string, and Java's equals of the values arrays and maps hold

AtlasType, ObjectIdType, EnumType, ArrayType and MapType move out of types.py, which re-exports them. In aurelius-atlas-model: the Atlas JSON codec (codec, DD-039), Java's map constructors of AtlasStruct, AtlasObjectId and AtlasRelatedObjectId, and to_json writing values as the codec needs them.

For each type: createDefaultValue, createOptionalDefaultValue, createDefaultValue(value), isValidValue, getNormalizedValue, validateValue, their ForUpdate variants and areEqualValues.

No endpoint changes; nothing validates entities yet.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by The value side of struct, classification, entity, relationship and business metadata types 2.1c Attribute options checked on values (maxStrLength, validPattern), time boundaries 2.1c Reading request bodies with the codec in the REST layer 2.3, 2.4

items.title: Semantics
items.text:
"Java value" below means what Atlas's Jackson mapper reads from a REST body, and the values Atlas's code builds; DD-040 says how each is held in Python. A JSON integer is a Java Integer, Long or BigInteger by its size; a JSON number with a fraction or exponent is a BigDecimal (USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS).

Id Rule VAL-01 The Atlas JSON codec reads a body as Jackson does: objects in order, arrays, strings, integers exactly, every number with a fraction or exponent as a decimal with its digits, booleans and null. It writes a decimal with its digits (BigDecimal.toString: 1.10, 1E+3), a date as epoch milliseconds, a float as its shortest decimal, NaN as the string "NaN", and map keys as Java's text of the key; to_json leaves these values to it VAL-02 Every type: null is valid and normalises to null. validateValue of an invalid value adds <name>=<value>: invalid value for type <type>, the value in Java's text (String.valueOf). The ForUpdate variants are the plain ones except for arrays and maps (VAL-12, VAL-13). createDefaultValue(value) is the default for null, else the normalised value; the optional default is the default, except for string (VAL-09). Two values are equal when both are null, or both normalise and their normalised values are equal; a value that does not normalise equals nothing VAL-03 boolean: a boolean, or the string true or false in any case; default false VAL-04 byte, short, int and long: a number whose integer part, truncated toward zero, is in the type's range (a Java float or double converted as Java converts it, NaN as 0), normalised to that integer; or a string Java's valueOf parses: an optional sign and ASCII digits. Anything else, a boolean included, is invalid. Default 0 VAL-05 float and double: a number within ±Float.MAX_VALUE or ±Double.MAX_VALUE, normalised to a 32-bit or 64-bit float (a float written as the shortest decimal of its 32-bit value); or a string Java's valueOf parses (trimmed; sign; decimal or hexadecimal digits; exponent; NaN; Infinity; an f, F, d or D suffix) to a finite value. Two values are equal when their normalised values differ by less than 1e-8. Default 0 VAL-06 biginteger: a decimal or a string Java's BigDecimal parses, truncated toward zero; an integer as it is; a Java float or double converted to long as Java does. Default 0 VAL-07 bigdecimal: every number is valid. A decimal stays as it is and an integer beyond the long range becomes an exact decimal; 0 becomes 0, and any other number becomes BigDecimal.valueOf of its Java double (5 becomes 5.0). A string is valid when Java's BigDecimal parses it. Default 0 VAL-08 date: a number is the date that many milliseconds after the epoch (Java's long conversion). A string is parsed leniently as yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z' in UTC (fields roll over, text after the pattern is ignored), else as a long. An empty string is valid but normalises to null. Default the epoch VAL-09 string: every value is valid and normalises to Java's text of it: numbers as Java writes them, true, maps as {k=v, …}, lists as [a, b]. Default "", optional default null VAL-10 objectid: an object id, or a map with a non-empty guid, or with a non-empty typeName and a non-empty uniqueAttributes map. A map normalises to a related object id when it has a relationshipType key, else to an object id, as Java's map constructors read it. Default {"guid": "-1", "typeName": <object type>}. Two object ids are equal after mapping their GUIDs through the GUID assignments: by GUID when both or neither GUID is assigned (non-empty, not starting with -), else by type name and unique attributes VAL-11 An enum type: a value whose Java text equals an element's value, ignoring case, normalised to that element's value; default the enum's default value VAL-12 array<T>: a list whose size is within the minimum and maximum count, when set, and whose elements are valid. Normalising first parses a string as JSON (a string that is not a JSON array normalises to null), then normalises each element, keeping nulls; a wrong count or element normalises the whole array to null. validateValue adds <name>: incorrect number of values. found=<n>; expected: minCount=<min>, maxCount=<max> and validates each element as <name>[<i>]. The default holds the element's default once, or minCount times. A LIST equals element by element; a SET (each value once, Java equality) has the same size and each element equals one of the other's VAL-13 map<K,V>: a map whose keys and values are valid. Normalising first parses a string as JSON, then normalises keys and values, keeping null values; an invalid key or value normalises the whole map to null. validateValue adds <name>.<key>: invalid key for type <type> and validates each value as <name>.<key>. The default maps the key's default to the value's, or is empty when the key has none. Null equals an empty map; otherwise equal maps have the same size and equal values by key VAL-14 AtlasStruct, AtlasObjectId and AtlasRelatedObjectId are made from a map as their Java map constructors do: a struct takes typeName and attributes, or the whole map when it has no attributes map; an object id takes guid, typeName and a uniqueAttributes map; a related object id adds relationshipGuid, relationshipType, relationshipStatus and relationshipAttributes as a struct VAL-15 Atlas's type tests hold: the valid, limit, negative and invalid values of TestAtlas{Boolean,Byte,Short,Int,Long,Float,Double,BigInteger,BigDecimal,Date,String,ObjectId}Type, TestAtlasArrayType and TestAtlasMapType, each Java value held as DD-040 says

items.title: 2.2 Entity store
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-043 to DD-048, DV-14 to DV-16; relies on ADR 023, ADR 047, DD-028 to DD-031, DD-039 to DD-041

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The entities' storage in Elasticsearch, in aurelius-atlas-core: what AtlasEntityStoreV2 and EntityGraphMapper keep in the graph, without the request logic around it, which 2.3 to 2.5 port. ADR 047 leaves the storage layout, the identifier strategy and the consistency model to the design log; this increment records them.

Module What it holds stored_entity StoredEntity: an entity as stored, its system properties and attribute values unique_key UniqueKey: one unique attribute value of one entity type, the id of its reservation entity_documents EntityDocuments and its Elasticsearch implementation: indices, reads, conditional writes, reservations, journal entity_store EntityStore: GUIDs, reads by GUID and unique attributes, all-or-nothing writes, recovery, type usage testing/memory MemoryEntityDocuments, for tests

The server builds the entity store at start-up, recovers interrupted writes, and gives the typedef store its type usage check (DD-030). It also answers GET /api/atlas/admin/patches, promised by 1.5 (DD-031).

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Reading entities over REST, with relationships and classifications (EntityGraphRetriever) 2.3 Creating and updating entities from requests: discovery, references, relationships (EntityGraphMapper) 2.4 Deleting entities: soft, hard and purge 2.5 Indexing attribute values for search (the attribute mapping) 4.1 A recorded migration mechanism for mapping changes that move data (ADR 023) when first needed

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule ENS-01 Entities live in one index behind the alias aurelius-atlas-entities, one document per entity with the GUID as its id; its system properties are mapped for exact lookup, its attribute values are stored but not indexed until 4.1 (DD-043). Unique value reservations and the write journal have an index each, aurelius-atlas-unique-values and aurelius-atlas-entity-journal. Preparing the store creates what is missing and changes nothing that exists ENS-02 A new entity's GUID is a random UUID in its canonical lower-case form, as Java's UUID.randomUUID() (DD-044) ENS-03 An entity is stored with its GUID, type name, every super type name, state, createTime and updateTime in epoch milliseconds, createdBy and updatedBy, version, isIncomplete, provenanceType, homeId, labels, custom attributes and attribute values. Attribute values are stored under the attribute's qualified name (Referenceable.qualifiedName) as the codec writes them (DD-039). Creating sets both times to the request's time and the state to ACTIVE; version is the entity's own, never incremented by the store (getEntityVersion) ENS-04 Entities are read by GUID, one or many, as last written: a read never waits for an index refresh. An unknown GUID reads as nothing ENS-05 An ACTIVE entity holds one reservation for each unique attribute with a value: of its entity type, the attribute's qualified name and the normalised value (PER_TYPE_UNIQUE). A write that needs a value another entity holds fails, writing nothing, with an error naming the value and its holder; Atlas fails such a write with an internal error (AtlasSchemaViolationException), and 2.4 decides the answer to a request. A value is released when the entity changes it, or leaves ACTIVE (removeProperty(uniquePropertyName) on delete) (DD-045) ENS-06 An entity is found by unique attributes: the ACTIVE entity of the type holding every given unique value; else, for a type with sub types, of the first sub type that has one (findByUniqueAttributes). Values of attributes that are not unique, and null values, are ignored; none left finds nothing ENS-07 A write is a batch of new and changed entities, all or nothing (DD-046): every reservation and check is made before any entity is written; a failure during the write restores every entity written to its state before; a write interrupted by a crash is undone by the next recovery. A reader may see part of a write while it is being written (DV-16) ENS-08 A changed entity is written only over the state it was read in; another process's write in between fails the batch with a version conflict, for the caller to read again and retry (DD-047) ENS-09 A type is in use while an entity of it exists, in any state (typeHasInstanceVertex); the typedef store asks before deleting a type (DD-030, DD-048) ENS-10 GET /admin/patches answers {"patches": [...]}, the patch records of the typedef document (DD-031) sorted by id, each as AtlasPatch writes it; Atlas's Java patches are not among them (DV-14)

items.text: DV-14: Atlas also records its Java patches (JAVA_PATCH_0000_001, …), which repair JanusGraph and Solr indexes and have nothing to repair in Elasticsearch; admin/patches lists the typedef patches only. DV-15: an entity's createdBy and updatedBy name the logged-in user in Atlas; until 6.1 they are absent, as for type definitions (DV-04, DV-06). DV-16: Atlas commits a request's entities in one graph transaction, which no reader sees half done; here a reader may see part of a multi-entity write for the duration of its bulk request (DD-046).

items.title: 2.3 Entity read REST
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: –
  • Records: DD-049 to DD-051, DV-17 to DV-19; relies on DD-039, DD-040, DD-043 to DD-047, DV-15

items.title: Scope
items.text:
The read endpoints of EntityREST under /api/atlas/v2/entity, on the entity store of 2.2: Atlas's EntityGraphRetriever and the read methods of AtlasEntityStoreV2.

Endpoint Answers GET guid/{guid} AtlasEntityWithExtInfo GET guid/{guid}/header AtlasEntityHeader GET uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}?attr:<name>=<value> AtlasEntityWithExtInfo GET uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/header?attr:<name>=<value> AtlasEntityHeader GET bulk/uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}?attr_<n>:<name>=<value> AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo GET bulk?guid=<guid>&guid=… AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo

In aurelius-atlas-core, entity_retriever (EntityRetriever) builds entities and headers from stored ones; the server's routes/entity answers the endpoints. StoredEntity gains isProxy, which Atlas stores and reads back.

Not in scope:

Not delivered here Delivered by Creating and updating entities over REST, and scenarios that create what they read (DD-051) 2.4 Relationship attribute values (relationshipAttributes hold none until relationships are stored) 3.1 Classifications of an entity (classifications, classificationNames), guid/{guid}/classifications 3.3 bulk/headers (headers by classification update time) 3.4 Audit events ({guid}/audit) 3.5 Meanings (glossary terms) and business attributes of an entity 5.2, 5.3 Access checks (ENTITY_READ) 6.2

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule ERD-01 A GUID or type name in the path, and each guid of bulk, longer than 4096 characters fails with INVALID_QUERY_PARAM_LENGTH (400) before anything is read (Servlets.validateQueryParamLength) ERD-02 guid/{guid} answers the entity with that GUID, in any state, with its extended info; an unknown GUID fails with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND (404). bulk answers the entities of every guid given, in order, sharing one referredEntities; one unknown GUID fails the request, and no guid fails with INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND naming [] ERD-03 An entity has its system properties as stored: guid, typeName, status, version, createTime, updateTime, proxy, isIncomplete, provenanceType, and homeId, createdBy, updatedBy and customAttributes when it has them; labels always, empty or not. classifications, meanings, businessAttributes and pendingTasks are left out (3.3, 5.2, 5.3) ERD-04 attributes holds every attribute of the entity's type, inherited ones included, null when the entity has no value (mapAttributes). A date reads as epoch milliseconds, an enum as its value, a struct as an AtlasStruct with every attribute of its type, arrays and maps as their elements read so (DD-049) ERD-05 An attribute that refers to entities reads each as an object id: GUID, type name and the referenced entity's unique attribute values that are not null. An owned reference (ownedRef) reads as GUID and type name only and adds the referenced entity to referredEntities: in full, or with minExtInfo=true with its system properties and those of its type's minimal-info attributes that have a value. An entity is built once per response, the first way it is reached. A reference to an entity that does not exist, and a null element of an array or map of references, reads as nothing (DD-049) ERD-06 Unless ignoreRelationships=true, relationshipAttributes names every relationship attribute of the type: null for a SINGLE end and [] for a LIST or SET end, as an entity without relationships reads (DD-050). referredEntities never holds the entities the response answers with (compact) ERD-07 guid/{guid}/header answers the entity's header: typeName, guid, status, isIncomplete, labels, classificationNames and classifications empty, meanings and meaningNames empty, each header attribute (the unique ones, name, description, owner, createTime) with its value or "", and displayText: the type's display text attribute, else name, displayName, qualifiedName, when one has a value (mapVertexToAtlasEntityHeader). The header by unique attributes is the same without classifications ERD-08 The unique attributes of uniqueAttribute reads are the query parameters attr:<name>, each with its first value; of bulk/uniqueAttribute, the parameters attr_<n>:<name>, one set per <n>, each with its first value; an attr_ parameter without : is ignored. An unknown entity type fails with TYPE_NAME_INVALID (400, ENTITY), no attribute or one that is not a unique attribute of the type, system attributes included, with ATTRIBUTE_UNIQUE_INVALID (400); the bulk read checks every set before reading any, and answers {} for none ERD-09 A read by unique attributes finds the ACTIVE entity of the type or of its first sub type holding the values, each normalised by its attribute's type (ENS-06); none fails with INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND (404) naming the type and the attributes as {name=value}. A unique system attribute (__guid) finds nothing (DV-17). The bulk read answers the sets in the order their indices first appear (DV-19) and leaves out those that find none ERD-10 Every endpoint reads from a registry no older than the refresh interval (TDS-13) and answers Atlas JSON (SRV-04, SRV-05)
